clue.text: Bonhomie displayed at the bar of the House?

definitions.text: Bonhomie displayed at the bar of the House?

parts.words: Bonhomie displayed at the bar of the House?
parts.note: the bar is both a drinks counter serving spirits and the rail of the House of Commons, where loyalty to a political party is on show

explanation.surface: Good cheer breaks out among MPs at the Commons bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar of the House is the boundary rail in Britain's House of Commons; read as a pub bar it serves spirits, and politicians belong to parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A friendly, convivial mood at a gathering is called this, and the clue adds the political party and the bar's drink.

clue.text: Eat sparingly and show the. way when commonly drunk

parts.note: to pick at food, or pick, is to eat only a little of it
led means guided or showed the way

explanation.surface: Advice on nibbling and leading the party home when tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show the way' gives LED, its past tense; 'commonly' says PICKLED is a colloquial word for drunk, and 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for intoxicated: someone well preserved in alcohol is said to be pickled.

clue.text: Vertiginous dances

parts.note: lively Scottish dances, and the verb for spinning or staggering with dizziness

explanation.surface: Dances that leave everyone giddy.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is a Scottish country dance and also what a dizzy person does: the head spins and the body staggers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lively Scottish country dances share their name with the staggering and spinning that come with giddiness.

clue.text: Loaf 'ready sliced 'makes one long for a drink

indicators.note: a sliced loaf is cut into pieces, so the letters of these two words are cut up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Ready-sliced bread somehow leads to a thirst; reads as a remark about a dry sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sliced' turns LOAF READY into the answer. A YARD OF ALE is a tall, narrow glass about three feet long, drunk from as a pub challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a very tall trumpet-shaped glass, roughly a yard in length, used for beer.

clue.text: It gives-a lead to racing drivers for' a start'.'

definitions.text: It gives-a lead to racing drivers for' a start

parts.words: It gives-a lead to racing drivers for' a start
parts.note: the front place on a motor-race starting grid, earned by the fastest qualifier

explanation.surface: Something that puts racing drivers ahead at the start of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The best spot on the starting grid literally gives its driver a lead from the very start.

clue.text: Expression of sorrow from Lulu half-cut with, rough Fleury

indicators.note: roughly handled, so the letters are knocked into a new order
half of the word Lulu is cut away, keeping its first two letters

explanation.surface: A tipsy singer and someone named Fleury share a sad look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' leaves LU from Lulu, and 'rough' rearranges LU with FLEURY. Half-cut also means tipsy, pulling the surface away from cutting a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with regret or sorrow is doing things in a rueful manner; the clue gives the feeling the adverb expresses.

clue.text: It's. back to front for a composer

indicators.note: the word to is placed at the front of the answer

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the letters of It's are turned to run back to front

explanation.surface: Something about a composer gets put back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses ITS to STI, and 'front' puts TO before it. Paolo Tosti was an Italian song composer of the Victorian era.
explanation.definitionFit: Francesco Paolo Tosti, an Italian writer of songs and teacher of singing to the British royal family.

clue.text: Obliged to worry constantly about a wild horse

parts.note: must means are obliged to

indicators.note: turned about, so the letters of the word for pestering are rearranged

parts.note: to nag is to pester or worry someone over and over

explanation.surface: Being forced to fret endlessly over an untamed horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges NAG to ANG, after MUST. This is an indirect anagram, a loose device in older puzzles.
explanation.definitionFit: A feral horse of the American plains, descended from Spanish stock.

clue.text: Breaker of more than one union law

definitions.text: Breaker of more than one union law

parts.words: Breaker of more than one union law
parts.note: someone who breaks the law by entering a second marriage, the union being matrimony, not a trade union

explanation.surface: A trade unionist who breaks more than one law of the union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union' suggests a trade union; here it is marriage, and the law broken is the ban on having more than one spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A person married to two spouses at once commits a crime by holding more than one marriage.

clue.text: Overheads invariably featured in sunshine holiday brochures

definitions.text: Overheads invariably featured in sunshine holiday brochures

parts.words: Overheads invariably featured in sunshine holiday brochures
parts.note: overheads are not running costs but what is above you: the sky shown in every travel advert

explanation.surface: Fixed costs always appear in holiday brochures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overheads' sounds like business costs, but the overheads in the photos are the cloudless sky above the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: Brochures for sunny resorts always picture an unclouded blue heaven above the beach.

clue.text: See 9
An-injury on-a leading rocky isle

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters of isle are shaken up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone hurt on a craggy island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocky' rearranges ISLE to LESI, then ON follows; 'a leading' is padding that the old clue left in.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound or damaged patch of tissue is a medical term for harm to the body.

clue.text: The height of Japanese tourism

parts.note: the height is literally a mountain, the tallest peak in Japan and its best-known sight

explanation.surface: The peak of the tourist trade in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'height' reads as 'high point', but it is the highest mountain in Japan, a famous tourist sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Fuji, Japan's tallest peak, is a classic destination for visitors.

clue.text: Exasperation Pluto might cause

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, also called Pluto
may means might, expressing possibility

explanation.surface: The planet Pluto could cause annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: Pluto is the underworld god, known as Dis; 'cause' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is distress or consternation, a feeling close to frustrated exasperation.

clue.text: Press into service in the Orient

explanation.definitionFit: To force a sailor into a ship's crew by trickery is to shanghai him; and Shanghai is a great Chinese port in the East.

clue.text: Rousing game on the banks of the Scheldt

definitions.text: on the banks of the Scheldt

explanation.walkthrough: Game here is birds, and to rouse them from cover is to flush them; the Scheldt is a river reaching the sea in the Netherlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Driving birds from cover to be shot is flushing them; Flushing is the English name for Vlissingen, a Dutch port at the mouth of the Scheldt.

clue.text: Plan to find a treasure under layers of rock

indicators.note: in a down answer the gem is placed below the rock layers

parts.note: strata are layers of rock
a gem is a treasure or jewel

explanation.surface: A scheme to dig up treasure beneath rock beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts GEM below STRATA in this down answer; 'to find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a scheme or ruse devised to gain an advantage.

clue.text: See 4
Dismissed but 'continued' at the crease

explanation.walkthrough: At the crease, the batsman's ground in cricket, being out by deflecting the ball onto your own wicket is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batsman who knocks the ball onto his own stumps is out this way; and to keep going is to carry on.

clue.text: Dog-end: that's flat

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog
the nose is the front end of something, as of an aircraft

explanation.surface: A cigarette stub, and it is flattened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog-end' is British slang for a cigarette butt, but here the hyphen joins two pieces: dog and end.
explanation.definitionFit: A short, flattened, upturned snout like a pug's is described with this compound.

clue.text: Boxed though not of medically high standard

explanation.walkthrough: Military medical grading put the fittest at A1; C-rated meant low fitness.
explanation.definitionFit: Packed in a wooden case is crated; and a C rating, not an A, marked a lower medical grade for fitness.

clue.text: Tear up notes on -revised story:

parts.note: D is a musical note
E is another musical note

indicators.note: revised means reworked, so the letters of story are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Ripping up notes about a story that has been rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' gives two of the musical notes A to G, D and E; 'revised' rearranges STORY to STROY; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To rip something to pieces is to wreck it entirely.

clue.text: Key to one acting in a big way

definitions.text: Key to one acting in a big way

parts.note: G is a musical key
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: acting done in an extravagant manner, so its letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Advice on playing the part of someone in a grand style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a big way' rearranges ACTING to GANTIC, after G and I; the whole clue also hints at the meaning, enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on a huge, giant scale is the sense: of enormous size.

clue.text: Diana in spritely form

indicators.note: Diana is given a new shape, so her letters are rearranged into a spirit of the water

explanation.surface: The goddess Diana takes the shape of a sprite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in spritely form' rearranges DIANA; the whole clue also defines it, a water sprite of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A water nymph of classical myth, living in a spring or stream, is a kind of sprite.

clue.text: To twist it is, a pain to the listener

indicators.note: twist means turn the letters of to and it is into a new order

explanation.surface: To twist it would hurt the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twist' rearranges TO IT IS; the definition says the condition causes earache.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the ear causes earache, so it hurts someone who hears.

clue.text: Hooker in the capital on foot

explanation.walkthrough: 'the capital' is Paris, so the second definition asks for the French word for a heel; 'Hooker' suggests a prostitute or rugby player but is a claw.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey's claw grips like a hook; and in Paris, the capital of France, the word means the heel of the foot.

clue.text: Liberal honorarium about right

indicators.note: about means around, so the payment goes around the letter for right

parts.note: a fee is a payment such as an honorarium

explanation.surface: A generous payment for a right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts FEE around R.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous or open-handed, as in being free with money.

clue.text: Nothing wrong with a sanctimonious ruminant…

parts.note: OK means all right, with nothing wrong
pi is short for pious, meaning sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A self-righteous cud-chewer that is all fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing' wants to be O, but 'Nothing wrong' together gives OK.
explanation.definitionFit: This forest animal of Central Africa, related to the giraffe, chews the cud.

clue.text: I put Reg in rural environment — not uniform in shape

indicators.note: Reg is put inside the rearranged rural
the rural setting is taken as a jumbled surrounding, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone moves a man named Reg to the countryside, and the result is lopsided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'environment' rearranges RURAL to RULAR, and 'in' puts REG inside it after I. The anagram signal is loose in this old clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacking symmetry or an even form is described as irregular.

clue.text: Extra cash for destroying enemy dragon

indicators.note: destroying breaks up the letters of enemy dragon so they can be rebuilt

explanation.surface: A bonus paid for slaying a hostile dragon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroying' rearranges ENEMY DRAGON.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus paid to workers for hazardous jobs.
